issues.display_title: Issue #137: Elevation API: return terrain elevation for lat/lng points
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Add an API on gothru-maps-frontend (maps.panorra.com) that takes one or more lat/lng points and returns the terrain elevation for each, read from a public DEM.

Context

Trail elevations today come from TourMkr panorama altitude or values typed by the trail creator in the PWA, so they can be 0, a default (720), or far off. A probe against AWS Terrain Tiles at the Gunung Pancar dev trail points matched two points within ±12 m; the others differ because the stored values or coordinates are wrong. An elevation API lets the PWA (or any client) look up real terrain heights.

API

GET  /api/elevation?lat={lat}&lng={lng}
POST /api/elevation   { "points": [ { "lat": number, "lng": number }, ... ] }   // 1..500 points

Response:

{ "points": [ { "lat": -6.6214, "lng": 106.9152, "elevation_m": 735 } ],
  "source": "AWS Terrain Tiles (SRTM)" }

Scope

  • Route handler in src/app/api/elevation.
  • DEM: AWS Terrain Tiles, terrarium encoding, zoom 14; points grouped per tile, each tile fetched once per request, tiles fetched in parallel.
  • Tiles cached in Redis, same pattern as /data/satelite.
  • Bilinear interpolation between the 4 nearest pixels.
  • Validation: lat −85..85, lng −180..180, 1..500 points; 400 with a clear message on bad input, 502 when a tile cannot be fetched.
  • CORS for Panorra origins (panorra.com, dev.panorra.com, local PWA).
  • Response includes the data source for attribution.

Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /api/elevation?lat=-6.6214&lng=106.9152 returns about 735 m.
  • POST with the 4 Gunung Pancar dev trail points returns about 735 / 741 / 550 / 852 m.
  • Invalid input returns 400; more than 500 points returns 400.
  • A repeated request for the same area is served from cache.

Notes

  • Accuracy is SRTM: coarse resolution, about ±16 m vertical. Fine for trail profiles, not survey-grade.
  • AWS Terrain Tiles needs attribution; no API key or published quota.
  • No rate limit, same as the satellite proxy.

RESULT

GET /api/elevation?lat=&lng= and POST /api/elevation { "points": [...] } (1..500 points) return { points: [{ lat, lng, elevation_m }], source: "AWS Terrain Tiles (SRTM)" }.

  • Code: src/app/api/elevation/route.ts (tile fetch, Redis cache, responses, CORS) and src/helpers/elevation.ts (tile math, terrarium decode, bilinear sampling, validation).
  • Tiles: terrarium zoom 14, grouped per request and fetched once each, in parallel; cached in Redis for 90 days (same TTL as the satellite proxy). X-Cache: HIT when every tile came from Redis, else MISS.
  • Elevation: bilinear between the 4 nearest pixel centers, rounded to whole meters (SRTM is about ±16 m).
  • Errors: 400 with a message for missing or out-of-range lat/lng, invalid JSON, 0 or more than 500 points, or points spanning more than 64 tiles; 502 when a tile cannot be fetched.
  • CORS: panorra.com, www.panorra.com, dev.panorra.com, localhost:4200, localhost:5200. GET responses carry Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400.

Checked:

  • tsc --noEmit and eslint pass; assert script for tile math, terrarium decode, bilinear sampling, edge clamping and validation (including missing params not becoming 0,0).
  • Dev server: GET trailhead -6.6214,106.9152 → 735 m; POST 4 Gunung Pancar points → 735 / 740 / 550 / 852 m; new area → X-Cache: MISS, repeat → HIT; 7 invalid inputs → 400; CORS preflight echoes allowed origins only.
  • Not verified: cache-hit latency on the production server. From the dev machine, Redis (192.168.1.106) is 272 ms RTT at about 9 KB/s, so a cached 114 KB tile takes about 10 s to read there; the satellite proxy shows the same pattern. On the server's LAN this should be milliseconds.
